documents.title: Optional Syllabus Statements for the Acceptable or Unacceptable Use of AI Tools in Your Course
documents.summary: A university-hosted set of optional sample syllabus statements adapted from Temple University, which instructors adjust to their course. The four samples range from broad permitted use with citation, through narrow permitted uses, to specific or total bans, with a placeholder for penalties.
documents.stance_why: The document gives no campus-wide rule; it says 'Please adjust the statement to reflect your parameters and to fit your course' and supplies samples from 'allowing broad use' to 'forbidding all use', so the decision is delegated to instructors and the samples are tiers.

units.why: Guidance tells instructors to be specific about permitted and not permitted class activities; 'Be specific and let students know' asks faculty to communicate expectations, so P09.
units.anchor: Be specific and let students know what class activities are permitted and not permitted

units.why: The document frames its samples as adjustable by each instructor ('adjust the statement to reflect your parameters'), so the rule is set per course, P04.
units.anchor: adjust the statement to reflect your parameters and to fit your course

units.why: Instructors who prohibit are told to 'think about the appropriate level of penalty' for first-time and repeat offenders; setting penalties in advance, P37.
units.anchor: think about the appropriate level of penalty for first-time offenders and those who repeatedly violate

units.why: Sample statement 1 says 'You are welcome to use generative AI tools', a broad default allowance, so P02.
units.anchor: You are welcome to use generative AI tools

units.why: The sample says students are 'responsible for the information you submit' including IP and misinformation; ownership of what is submitted is P29 (P31 fits less because the sentence is about responsibility, not checking).
units.anchor: You are responsible for the information you submit based on an AI query

units.why: 'must be properly documented and cited' under broad-use permission requires citing AI use, P24.
units.anchor: Your use of AI tools must be properly documented and cited

units.why: Unauthorized use is tied to a penalty placeholder: 'found to have used generative AI tools in unauthorized ways [insert the penalty here]'. A penalty stated in advance, P37.
units.anchor: Any assignment that is found to have used generative AI tools in unauthorized ways [insert

units.why: 'When in doubt about permitted usage, please ask for clarification' is the ask-first rule, P10.
units.anchor: When in doubt about permitted usage, please ask for clarification

units.why: Sample statement 2 permits AI 'only for the following activities', a narrow list set per course, so the rule is set by the instructor, P04.
units.anchor: permitted in this course only for the following activities

units.why: Brainstorming and refining ideas is a listed permitted use, P15.
units.anchor: Brainstorming and refining your ideas

units.why: Fine-tuning research questions is a listed permitted use; closest is exploring approaches, P15.
units.anchor: Fine tuning your research questions

units.why: Finding information on a topic is a permitted use akin to a search engine for understanding, P12.
units.anchor: Finding information on your topic

units.why: Drafting an outline is a permitted prose-structuring use, P18.
units.anchor: Drafting an outline to organize your thoughts

units.why: Checking grammar and style is a prose-support use, P18.
units.anchor: Checking grammar and style

units.why: Unacceptable statement 1 says the tools are 'not permitted in this class', a full ban, P01.
units.anchor: The use of generative AI tools (such as ChatGPT, DALL-E, etc.) is not permitted in
units.policy: The use of generative AI tools is not permitted in this class.

units.why: It classes any use under a full ban as a violation of the academic integrity policy 'since the work is not your own', P36.
units.anchor: may be considered a violation of CSULB's Policy on Academic Integrity Regarding Cheating and Plagiarism

units.why: 'The use of any AI tools will result in [insert the penalty here]' states a penalty in advance, P37.
units.anchor: The use of any AI tools will result in [insert the penalty here

units.why: Unacceptable statement 2 bans AI only 'for the following activities', so the ban is activity-level and set by the instructor, P04.
units.anchor: not permitted in this course for the following activities

units.why: Barred use: 'Impersonating you in classroom contexts' such as discussion board posts or Zoom chat content; this is student course communication, P58.
units.anchor: Impersonating you in classroom contexts
units.policy: Using generative AI tools to compose discussion board prompts assigned to you or content you put into a Zoom chat is not permitted.

units.why: Barred use: completing assigned group work with AI unless the group agrees; AI doing assigned work (P19) with a group-consent exception.

documents.title: AI Guidelines
documents.summary: Campus-wide guidelines from the Division of IT's AI Steering Committee for students, faculty and staff. They recommend four course policy levels, require disclosure when instructors allow AI, and set data-privacy, research and procurement rules.
documents.stance_why: The guidelines set no single campus rule on student AI use; they say 'Follow the instructor's requirements' and recommend faculty 'select one of the following course policy levels' (Prohibited, Limited, Permitted with Disclosure, Integrated), so the decision is delegated and the levels are tiers.

units.why: The preamble says CSULB 'supports the responsible and ethical use of artificial intelligence', an institution-level statement of purpose, P56.
units.anchor: supports the responsible and ethical use of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies

units.why: Scope sentence: the guidelines 'apply to all members of the CSULB community', defining scope, P56 (P61 is for definitions of AI).
units.anchor: These guidelines apply to all members of the CSULB community

units.why: Defines Generative AI as 'Tools that produce text, images, audio, video, code', setting the scope of terms, P61.
units.anchor: Tools that produce text, images, audio, video, code

units.why: Defines 'Sensitive Data' as information protected by FERPA, HIPAA, IRB and policies; a definition that scopes the data rules, P61.
units.anchor: Information protected by FERPA, HIPAA, IRB protocols, CSULB policies, or CSU regulations

units.why: Defines Disclosure as 'A clear statement identifying how and when AI tools were used', a definition, P61.
units.anchor: A clear statement identifying how and when AI tools were used

units.why: Faculty are told to 'Define course-level expectations for AI', so each course sets its rule, P04.
units.anchor: Define course-level expectations for AI, using sample syllabus language provided by CSULB

units.why: Students 'Follow the instructor's requirements regarding the use of AI'; the instructor sets the rule, P04.
units.anchor: Follow the instructor's requirements regarding the use of AI

units.why: If permitted, students 'disclose the use of AI' and cite it, P24.
units.anchor: If the instructor permits the use of AI, disclose the use of AI

units.why: 'If the instructor does not permit the use of AI in their classes, do not use AI' is a prohibition where the instructor bans it, P01.
units.anchor: If the instructor does not permit the use of AI in their classes, do not

units.why: Staff should 'Consult the appropriate administrator or supervisor before using AI'; decided locally by the supervisor, P04.
units.anchor: Consult the appropriate administrator or supervisor before using AI

units.why: Staff use must ensure 'compliance with data and security protocols', a data-protection duty, P50.
units.anchor: ensuring compliance with data and security protocols

units.why: Brainstorming and outlining is listed 'Allowed (with human oversight and disclosure)', P15.
units.anchor: Brainstorming and outlining

units.why: Grammar, translation and accessibility support allowed 'with verification', a prose-focused allowance, P18.
units.anchor: Grammar, translation, and accessibility support (with verification)

units.why: Administrative efficiency such as summarization and scheduling is allowed; staff operations use, P59.
units.anchor: Administrative efficiency (e.g., summarization, scheduling)

units.why: Handling sensitive data is 'Restricted (requires approval/secure tools)', P50.
units.anchor: Handling of sensitive data (FERPA/PII/PHI, research data)

units.why: Automated decision-making in grading and admissions 'must include human review'; human oversight of grading, P46.
units.anchor: Automated decision-making in admissions, grading, HR, or financial processes (must include human review)

units.why: Prohibited: uploading sensitive data to unapproved AI tools, P50.
units.anchor: Uploading University sensitive data to unapproved AI tools

units.why: Prohibited: fabricating or falsifying data, citations, or sources; closest is the verify-output type P31, but it forbids fabrication rather than requiring checks.
units.anchor: Fabricating or falsifying data, citations, or sources

units.why: Prohibited: 'Misrepresenting AI-generated work as entirely one's own when prohibited', so students may not pass off AI work as their own, P19.
units.anchor: Misrepresenting AI-generated work as entirely one's own when prohibited

units.why: Prohibited: using AI to create harmful, discriminatory or illegal content, an ethics rule, P53.
units.anchor: Using AI to create harmful, discriminatory, or illegal content

units.why: 'Faculty should clearly define their AI usage policy in each course syllabus' requires a syllabus AI statement, P09.
units.anchor: Faculty should clearly define their AI usage policy in each course syllabus

units.why: Detectors 'should not be used as sole evidence of misconduct'; not relying on detectors alone, P39.
units.anchor: AI detection tools (e.g.: Turnitin AI detection) should not be used as sole evidence of

units.why: Faculty are recommended to pick one of four named levels (Prohibited, Limited, Permitted with Disclosure, Integrated), P05.
units.anchor: Faculty are recommended to select one of the following course policy levels regarding use of

units.why: Level 'Prohibited': AI not allowed in coursework, P01.
units.anchor: AI use is not allowed in coursework

units.why: Level 'Limited': only specific uses such as formatting and grammar checking with citation; defines a named tier, P05.
units.anchor: Only specific uses (e.g., formatting, grammar checking etc.) are allowed with proper citation

units.why: Level 'Permitted with Disclosure': drafting and summarization allowed with citation; a named tier, P05.
units.anchor: AI can be used for drafting/summarization with proper citation

units.why: Level 'Integrated': AI 'is required and embedded into assignments'; a named tier, P05, with unit stance require.
units.anchor: AI is required and embedded into assignments

units.why: Students 'Consult with their instructor about usage of AI in each class', ask first, P10.
units.anchor: Consult with their instructor about usage of AI in each class

units.why: If permitted, students 'disclose tool name, purpose, and scope of AI use', a specific detail requirement, P25.
units.anchor: disclose tool name, purpose, and scope of AI use

units.why: Students 'verify accuracy' of AI content and cite it, P31.
units.anchor: Carefully review AI content, verify accuracy, and provide citations

units.why: Students must review AI content for bias and discriminatory outcomes; a student duty to check output, P31 rather than P53.
units.anchor: Review AI generated content for bias, inaccuracies, favoritism, prejudice, and discriminatory outcomes

units.why: Research: 'Use only Microsoft CoPilot and ChatGPT provided by CSULB' names the sanctioned tools, P17.
units.anchor: Use only Microsoft CoPilot and ChatGPT provided by CSULB

units.why: Research: 'Follow IRB and sponsor guidelines', deferring to external rules, P62.
units.anchor: Follow IRB and sponsor guidelines

units.why: Research: 'Do not upload restricted data/code to consumer AI platforms' is about data protection in research, P50 (P20 is about assignment specs).
units.anchor: Do not upload restricted data/code to consumer AI platforms

units.why: Research: 'Attribute AI contributions in publications per disciplinary standards', P62.
units.anchor: Attribute AI contributions in publications per disciplinary standards

units.why: Research: 'Document model versions, prompts, and limitations' names specific citation details, P25 (P62 is research governance but this names tool and prompt).
units.anchor: Document model versions, prompts, and limitations when relevant to reproducibility

units.why: Privacy: 'Never upload sensitive data to unapproved tools', P50.
units.anchor: Never upload sensitive data to unapproved tools

units.why: 'Use campus-approved AI platforms when available' prefers vetted tools, P50.
units.anchor: Use campus-approved AI platforms when available

units.why: 'Apply data minimization and anonymization where possible', P50.
units.anchor: Apply data minimization and anonymization where possible

units.why: 'Report suspected data breaches to CSULB DOIT immediately' is a data-protection duty, P50.
units.anchor: Report suspected data breaches to CSULB DOIT immediately

units.why: AI-generated captions, transcripts and alt text must be 'reviewed for accuracy'; closest is verifying output, P31.
units.anchor: Ensure AI-generated content (captions, transcripts, alt text) is reviewed for accuracy

units.why: 'Avoid reliance on tools that are not ADA compliant' is an equity/access rule, P51.
units.anchor: Avoid reliance on tools that are not ADA compliant

units.why: 'Apply universal design principles to all AI-supported materials', an access rule, P51.
units.anchor: Apply universal design principles to all AI-supported materials

units.why: 'Use CSU/CSULB procurement processes for new AI tools', a vendor review rule, P65.
units.anchor: Use CSU/CSULB procurement processes for new AI tools

units.why: Evaluate privacy, accessibility and security compliance of vendors, P65.
units.anchor: Evaluate privacy, accessibility, and security compliance

units.why: 'Prefer vendors offering transparency on data usage and storage', P65.
units.anchor: Prefer vendors offering transparency on data usage and storage

units.why: Workshops and consultations are offered by ATS for students, faculty and staff; support for learning AI, P63.
units.anchor: Workshops, consultations, and resources are offered by ATS for students, faculty, and staff

units.why: Students who do not conform are 'Subject to University policies, including those regarding student conduct', handled through conduct processes, P36.
units.anchor: Subject to University policies, including those regarding student conduct

units.why: Faculty and staff nonconformity is 'Subject to relevant University policies', the same enforcement hook for employees, P36.
units.anchor: Subject to relevant University policies

units.why: The AI Steering Committee 'Oversees campus-wide AI guidelines', who maintains the framework, P56.
units.anchor: Oversees campus-wide AI guidelines

documents.title: Student Guidelines on Generative AI
documents.summary: Student-facing page that tells students to follow each instructor's syllabus and to ask before using AI. It describes three instructor scenarios (broad use, specific use, forbidden), requires citation of allowed AI use, and warns of discipline for unauthorized use.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no universal permission or ban; it says 'Instructors' expectations can vary by course' and walks through three cases (allow broad use, allow specific use, forbid), while 'DO NOT use GenAI unless you have received an OK' only supplies a fallback, so the document delegates to instructors.

units.why: The page says GenAI is 'most effective when it supports learning and growth rather than replacing the effort', a rationale for limits, P41.
units.anchor: supports learning and growth rather than replacing the effort required to attain deeper insights

units.why: The page names training-data, energy and bias concerns tied to CSULB's equity and sustainability commitments, P53.
units.anchor: require substantial energy to operate, and may reflect biases present in the training data

units.why: 'students must communicate with them' before using AI for coursework: ask first, P10.
units.anchor: students must communicate with them to understanding how AI may be used appropriately before using

units.why: Where broad use is allowed, AI use 'must be properly documented and cited', P24.
units.anchor: your use of AI tools must be properly documented and cited

units.why: Unauthorized use 'may result in academic disciplining, and a lower, or failing grade', unauthorized AI use as misconduct, P36 (penalty stated only loosely, so not P37).
units.anchor: may result in academic disciplining, and a lower, or failing grade

units.why: 'be sure to seek clarification and guidance from your instructor' on any doubtful assignment, P10.
units.anchor: be sure to seek clarification and guidance from your instructor

units.why: Instructors may allow specific uses (brainstorming, research questions, outline, grammar); per-instructor narrow permission, P04.
units.anchor: your instructor may allow usage of generative AI tools for brainstorming, and refining ideas

units.why: Permitted AI 'also includes AI features built into existing software packages (e.g. Microsoft Copilot)', so embedded AI is covered, P07.
units.anchor: AI features built into existing software packages (e.g. Microsoft Copilot)

units.why: 'seek clear guidance from your instructor BEFORE you use generative AI', P10.
units.anchor: seek clear guidance from your instructor BEFORE you use generative AI in your coursework

units.why: A full prohibition bars even 'partial or specific usage' for coursework, P01.
units.anchor: your instructor may fully prohibit the usage of GenAI

units.why: Examples barred under a ban include composing discussion posts or Zoom chat content, which is course communication, P58.
units.anchor: usage of generative AI to compose discussion posts, or create content for Zoom chats

units.why: Examples under a ban include writing assignment drafts or full and partial sentences and paragraphs, P19.
units.anchor: writing full and or partial sentences and paragraphs for class assignments and submissions

units.why: 'DO NOT use GenAI unless you have received an OK from your instructor' sets a fallback: no AI without permission, P06.
units.anchor: DO NOT use GenAI unless you have received an OK from your instructor

units.why: Prohibited or unauthorized GenAI work 'may be subject to academic disciplining and a lower, or failing grade', P36.
units.anchor: may be subject to academic disciplining and a lower, or failing grade

units.why: Even when AI work is allowed, 'those contributions must be cited. If they are not, it may still be considered plagiarism': nondisclosure is itself a violation, P28.

units.why: The page says 'this document will be updated based on any changes in technology, and University policies', P54.

documents.title: AI for Teaching and Learning
documents.summary: A faculty-facing page from the Division of IT on benefits and concerns of AI in teaching, tips for introducing AI, and campus tools. It asks instructors to put a syllabus statement in place, advises against using unapproved detectors, and lists AI tools for instructors.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no student rule of its own; it advises 'Provide a statement in your syllabus' stating what is 'permitted and not permitted', which hands the decision to instructors, and otherwise mixes encouragement of AI use with cautions, so it delegates.

units.why: The page says AI use prepares students because 'Generative AI tools are or will be commonly used in workplaces', a career rationale, P44.
units.anchor: Generative AI tools are or will be commonly used in workplaces

units.why: Faculty are encouraged to use AI for examples, analogies and simple explanations of concepts, an instructor teaching use, P59.
units.anchor: Consider using AI to provide examples, analogies, and simple explanations

units.why: Educators can use AI to clarify and expand feedback to students, P59 (feedback drafting).
units.anchor: Educators can use AI to clarify and expand on their feedback to students

units.why: 'Faculty can encourage students to get immediate feedback from AI on their work' encourages student self-checking, P14.
units.anchor: Faculty can encourage students to get immediate feedback from AI on their work

units.why: AI-generated culturally relevant examples 'should be fact-checked', verifying output, P31.
units.anchor: It should be fact-checked, by corroborating the example with a trusted source

units.why: AI as 'a personal tutor' with a Socratic-tutor prompt: AI as tutor for understanding, P12.
units.anchor: Access a personal tutor

units.why: 'AI is great for brainstorming new ideas' for revising a course, an instructor use, P59.
units.anchor: AI is great for brainstorming new ideas

units.why: AI can let students with disabilities participate more fully (read aloud, to-do list), an access benefit, P51.
units.anchor: AI technologies, when used in the right way, can allow students with disabilities participate more

units.why: Dependency risks: 'a decline in critical thinking and problem-solving abilities', P41.
units.anchor: a decline in critical thinking and problem-solving abilities

units.why: Dependence 'can leave students unprepared for real-world situations', a warning about missing skills, P41.
units.anchor: dependence on AI can leave students unprepared for real-world situations

units.why: The page says the text was 'produced with the help of Chat GPT and reviewed by an instructional designer', disclosing AI-made content and its review, P48.
units.anchor: Text produced with the help of Chat GPT and reviewed by an instructional designer

units.why: AI 'may not be the correct answer' and users must examine responses; verify output, P31.
units.anchor: users will have to be aware of potential incorrect or made-up answers and examine the

units.why: Users 'may unintentionally upload sensitive information', raising privacy and security questions, P50.
units.anchor: users may unintentionally upload sensitive information to the AI's database

units.why: Intellectual property loss is a risk as laws 'are still evolving', P52.
units.anchor: it's important to be mindful of the potential for intellectual property loss

units.why: Faculty are advised to 'Teach students how AI is applied in a professional context', P44.
units.anchor: Teach students how AI is applied in a professional context

units.why: Faculty should teach limitations: AI 'can be inaccurate and even invent information', P31.
units.anchor: AI can be inaccurate and even invent information

units.why: Faculty should teach that AI can be used unethically (fake news, deep fakes), P53.
units.anchor: AI can be used unethically

units.why: 'Provide a statement in your syllabus' with specifics on permitted and not permitted activities, P09.
units.anchor: Provide a statement in your syllabus

units.why: Instructors who prohibit AI should 'clearly state the penalty' for first-time and repeat offenders, P37.
units.anchor: clearly state the penalty for first-time offenders and those who repeatedly violate your policies

units.why: Custom ChatGPT tools built for faculty (LOVE, quiz generator, rubric builder) support instructor teaching work, P59 (P17 is for student-facing tools).
units.anchor: tools developed by ATS Instructional Designers to support CSULB faculty

units.why: CSULB Co-Research Agent is a campus-provided tool that helps students develop research questions, P17.
units.anchor: helps students develop focused, academically rigorous research questions and literature review strategies

units.why: Instructors can estimate originality with Turnitin AI Detection in Canvas, P40.
units.anchor: instructors can estimate the originality of work using Turnitin with AI Detection

units.why: 'educators should not use other available AI detectors' because inputting student work 'could result in a FERPA violation'; the reason is student data, so P50 rather than P39.
units.anchor: educators should not use other available AI detectors

units.why: 'Before challenging students about the originality of their work, please review' false-positive guidance: check before escalating, P57.
units.anchor: Before challenging students about the originality of their work, please review these links

units.why: IgniteAI in Canvas Discussions summarizes themes and misconceptions for instructors; instructor AI use, P59.
units.anchor: summarizes key themes, questions, and helps to identify misconceptions and plan follow-up instruction

units.why: Microsoft Assignments can help generate assignment instructions, rubrics and feedback, instructor use, P59.
units.anchor: Microsoft Assignments can help generate assignment instructions and rubrics

units.why: After the Zoom AI summary, instructors should 'review and edit the summary for accuracy' before posting, reviewing AI-made materials, P48.
units.anchor: review and edit the summary for accuracy, add links or clarifications

units.why: AI summaries 'should supplement—not replace—student notes or approved note-taking accommodations', protecting accommodations, P51.
units.anchor: should supplement—not replace—student notes or approved note-taking accommodations
